compiled_state.title: Update project documentation to reflect Inputs dimension, assumption category, structural marker, and decision tree changes
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Update existing project documentation to reflect the new Inputs dimension, assumption category, structural marker convention, and inverted decision tree.

**Why**: Future agents need accurate awareness of the new pipeline shape. Stale docs silently propagate the old mental model and undo the cemented-premise gains.

**Scope**:
- IN: Update CLAUDE.md Architecture section if relevant (brainstorm pipeline summary); update plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md quick-reference table if relevant; update CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md if config keys added (none expected for this epic); update KNOWN-ISSUES.md if relevant; follow .claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md for formatting.
- OUT: New documentation files; net-new patterns; sibling-epic doc reconciliation (concurrent-edit handling is per-PR-rebase concern).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, all relevant existing project documentation files (CLAUDE.md, plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md, CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, KNOWN-ISSUES.md) are updated to reflect the Inputs dimension, assumption category, structural marker convention, and inverted decision tree, verified by manual review and `make lint-docs` (if available) passing.
  ← Satisfies: "documentation accuracy"
- When this story is complete, all updated documentation conforms to .claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md formatting and structure conventions.
  ← Satisfies: "documentation accuracy"

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Follow .claude/docs/DOCUMENTATION-GUIDE.md for documentation formatting, structure, and conventions.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
